# Code review

Review the pull request against this repository's own sources of truth. The rules below point at them and add what
they don't say. Every finding cites the file and rule it rests on.

## Sources of truth

Read the sections that govern the changed code before commenting on it:

- `CLAUDE.md` and `src/AtelierStore.Web/CLAUDE.md`: architecture, configuration, Central Package Management, and code
  style. They win when another instruction file disagrees.
- `.editorconfig`: tabs, explicit types over `var`, and `System` usings first.
- `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`: Blazor, .NET, Markdown, and blog post rules.
- `.github/instructions/git-commit-instructions.md`: commit message format.

## What to check

**Data access.** Components read products only through `Catalog/ProductCatalog.cs`, which creates one short-lived
`AppDbContext` per query and projects into the `Catalog.Product` view record. Flag a component that injects
`AppDbContext`, a query that returns tracked entities to the UI, or a projection that assumes an optional
relationship (such as `ProductStock`) is always present.

**Schema and seed data.** An entity, configuration, or `Data/CatalogSeedData.cs` change needs a matching migration
under `src/AtelierStore.Web/Migrations/`. `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes` must report none.

**Security.** Redirect targets (such as the login `returnUrl`) must be root-relative paths, never scheme-relative
(`//host`, `/\host`) or absolute URLs. Configuration comes from `.env` and environment variables; flag secrets in code
or `appsettings.json`. `<AuthorizeView>` isn't a security boundary; protected pages need `[Authorize]`.

**Rendering.** Pages render statically unless they declare a render mode. Flag an interactive render mode added where a
static form (`@formname` or `EditForm` with `FormName`) would do, and a missing record that doesn't call
`NavigationManager.NotFound()`.

**Styling.** New UI uses the design system in `Styles/app.css` (tokens and `@layer components` primitives) and stays
consistent with existing pages. Classes used outside `Components/` aren't generated by Tailwind.

**Tests.** There is no test project yet. When one exists, every new or changed behaviour has a test, following the
Testing section of `dotnet-project.instructions.md`. Until then, note behaviour that would need one.

**Markdown.** Lines outside tables stay within 200 characters; table rows can't wrap, so they're exempt. CI's
markdownlint enforces this and the other rules in `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`, except in the paths it ignores, such as
the generated posts in `docs/blogs/`.

**Workflows and hooks.** Steps that publish anything (open a PR, push, tag, release) run only for `main`: a
`github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` check, or a merged-into-`main` condition as in `release.yml`. `workflow_dispatch`
runs on any branch, and pull request runs check out a detached merge commit. Branch names in hooks and docs follow
`feature/{issue}-{slug}`, `fix/{issue}-{slug}`, `hotfix/{issue}-{slug}` or `chore/{slug}`. The job named `Build Solution` in `ci.yml` is a
required status check on `main`, so it must run on every pull request.

## Out of scope

Leave compiler errors to the build, and Central Package Management rejects a `Version` on a `PackageReference`.
Spend comments on behaviour, boundaries, tests and intent.
